title: Geo failsafe: leaky-bucket shedding with tiered circuit fallback
author: Asha Menon
release_notes: Adds a geo-aware leaky-bucket load-shedding policy and a lightweight tiered circuit fallback for cross-region failovers. Safe rollout: config off by default; feature flag + canary to 10% of traffic. No API changes.
description:
Motivation: During the recent geo-flare incidents we observed correlated tail-latency spikes that caused large-scale circuit trips in remote regions, taking down whole availability groups. This PR introduces a geo-aware leaky-bucket shedding layer upstream of the existing circuit-breaker so we can (1) smooth incoming bursts, (2) shed graded traffic when capacity is overwhelmed, and (3) only escalate to full circuit trips for persistent backend failures.

Design summary: single continuous description below. Key ideas: 1) Leaky-bucket queue per region+priority that drains at a configured token rate derived from SLO budget and observed service RPS. 2) Tiered circuit fallback: when the bucket exceeds a soft-threshold we switch degraded routing to a nearline-compatible model variant; only after a longer window of failures do we open a hard circuit. 3) Cross-region harmonization: local buckets are preferred, but a lightweight probe/scoreboard tracks neighboring region health and allows ephemeral reroutes under stringent limits. 4) Config + feature flags: all behavior is gated under feature.geo_leakybucket, with runtime knobs for drain_rate, soft_threshold, hard_threshold, fail_window_seconds, and remote_reroute_fraction.

Checklist:
- [x] Leaky-bucket implementation (runtime/eviction/leaky_bucket.go)
- [x] Tiered circuit bridge (runtime/circuit/tiered_bridge.go)
- [x] Config and feature flag plumbing (config/feature_flags.go, config/geo_shedding.yaml.example)
- [x] Unit tests for bucket accounting and failover heuristics (runtime/eviction/leaky_bucket_test.go)
- [x] Integration test that simulates region overload and asserts graceful degradation (test/integration/geo_shedding_integration.go)
- [x] Docs: design note and runbook updates (docs/reliability/geo-shedding.md)

Changes are additive to the runtime surface and do not change public API. The rollout plan in the linked Linear item ENG-1189 recommends: enable feature flag in staging, canary to 5% then 10% (region-scoped), monitor SLO regressions and tracing spans (new tag geo_shedding=true), then global enable.

How to test locally: start a local runtime with the example config and run the integration harness: `go test ./test/integration -run TestGeoShedding -count=1`. The integration harness includes a fault injector that can simulate backend error spikes and latency inflations so the bucket fills and triggers the tiered fallback.

Operational notes: When the soft threshold is hit the system will emit metric `geo_shedding.soft_threshold_events{region=\"<r>\"}` and when the hard threshold triggers the existing circuit-breaker metric will be tagged with `escalation=\"tiered\"`. A short code excerpt (illustrative only):

`// drain tokens at configured rate; if pending > softThreshold => route to nearline; if past failWindow => open hard circuit`

Motivation links: internal runbook https://redwood.internal/runbooks/geo-shedding, Linear ENG-1189, and the postmortem for incident 2026-01-29 (see SUP-342).

Risk and mitigations: The primary risk is over-eager shedding that could reduce throughput unnecessarily; mitigated by conservative default drain_rate and canary-first rollout. The bucket accounting is deterministic and covered by unit tests.

Merge notes: small follow-up change to sampling rate for traces was squashed into the final commit to keep span tag behavior consistent across releases.

review_comments: Dmitri Kovalev: Overall design LGTM. A couple of nits: please document units for drain_rate (tokens/sec) and ensure default values are conservative. Also add a comment explaining why remote_reroute_fraction is capped at 5%.
Asha Menon (author): Added explicit units and capped remote_reroute_fraction to 3% by default in config example (commit b2e9a6f). Also expanded docs to explain tradeoff.
Priya Shah: Can you add an invariant check in leaky_bucket to detect negative tokens (defensive)? We saw a similar bug previously during racey metric resets.
Asha Menon: Added invariant assert and unit test case that simulates concurrent resets (commit d4f1e0b).
Michael Tran: Integration test is useful but long-running in CI. Can we add a fast path unit test that exercises the bridge logic?
Asha Menon: Added a focused unit test and added a smoke CI job for faster feedback (scripts/ci/geo_shedding_smoke.sh).
Priya Shah: APPROVED (after small nit fixes)

notes_for_ops: If enabling in production, start with region-limited canary (10% traffic) and watch metrics geo_shedding.soft_threshold_events and circuit.open_count with tag escalation=tiered. If SLO regressions appear, increase drain_rate or reduce remote_reroute_fraction. Runbook link: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/geo-shedding
